::: {.lead}
Today you practise the safe and honest use of an AI tool, as in Lectures 17
and 18. There are no new ideas. **Part A** is in an AI assistant and Word
on the lab computer; **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive page:
on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step,
write your result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word, a browser and an AI assistant
  that the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your
  university account).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Word.
- **All names and numbers here are made up.** Never paste real personal
  data into an AI tool.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · Settings, rules and copyright

**The idea (Lecture 17):** before you use an AI tool, check its
**settings** (is the chat history saved? are your chats used for training?
switch it off if you can), use the **university account** for course work,
follow the AI rules of the course, and read the **terms of use**. Upload
only files that you may share.

**Aim:** check the settings and the rules of the AI tool that you use.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant)**
:::

1. Open the AI assistant that you use and find its settings (often under
   your picture or the menu ☰). Is the chat history saved? Can you switch
   off the use of your chats for training? Which account are you signed in
   with?

   {{< record "History … ; training … ; my account …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The answers depend on the tool. A good answer names the tool and the
   account (for example the university account in Copilot), says if the
   history is saved, and if training can be switched off. With a university
   account, your chats are protected by the university's agreement.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A tool uses your chats to improve its model. What do you do?

   - [x] Switch the training off, if you can.

     Why: Then your chats are not used to train the tool.

   - [ ] Paste more personal data, so that it learns you.

     Why: Personal data never goes into an AI tool.

   - [ ] Nothing: training is always fine.

     Why: Check the settings and switch training off if you can.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-11/sims/responsible-or-not.html" poster="../../week-11/sims/responsible-or-not.png" title="Responsible or Not? Six people, six AI tasks" kind="game" >}}

2. Play **Responsible or Not?**. What should Huda do: her AI tool saves all
   chats and uses them for training, and she wants to paste customer
   complaints with names?

   {{< record "Huda should …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Switch off training and anonymize the complaints**: no names in the
   prompt, and no chats used for training.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Your university gives you an account for an AI tool. Which account do
   you use for course work?

   - [x] the university account

     Why: It follows the rules and the agreement of the university.

   - [ ] a friend's account

     Why: Never use another person's account.

   - [ ] any free account without a sign-in

     Why: Use the account that the university gives you.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A safe prompt and an AI-use statement

**The idea (Lectures 17 and 18):** find every personal, sensitive or
confidential part of a prompt and replace it with a placeholder; keep what
the AI needs; add the real details later, in Word. Then check the answer,
make it sound like you, and write an **AI-use statement**: the tool, what
it did, what you changed and how you checked it.

**Aim:** use a safe prompt, finish the text in Word, and state the AI use.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. Make this prompt safe, then send it: *Write a thank-you message to our
   customer Salma Odeh (phone 0791 222 333) for her order of 12 boxes of
   tea for her office party.* Paste the answer into Word and add the real
   name yourself.

   {{< record "My safe prompt" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A safe prompt: "Write a thank-you message to [Customer] for her order of
   12 boxes of tea for her office party." The phone number goes; the order
   stays, because the AI needs it. You add *Ms Odeh* in Word.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which part of the prompt may stay?

   - [x] 12 boxes of tea for her office party

     Why: The AI needs the order, and it does not say who the customer is.

   - [ ] Salma Odeh

     Why: A name goes; use [Customer].

   - [ ] phone 0791 222 333

     Why: A phone number is personal data.
   :::

2. Edit the message so that it sounds like you, and check it. Under it,
   write an AI-use statement of three or four sentences.

   {{< record "My statement" lines=3 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   For example: "I used Microsoft Copilot to write a first thank-you
   message. I sent it no personal data and added the customer's name
   myself. I changed two sentences into my own words and checked the order
   details." It names the tool, the use, the changes and the check.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which part of a statement is each sentence? Sort them.

   The tool and the use
   :   I used an AI chat tool for a first thank-you message.

       Why: It names the tool and what it did.

   What you changed
   :   I rewrote two sentences in my own words.

       Why: It says what is yours.

   How you checked it
   :   I checked the order details against the shop's list.

       Why: It says how you checked the AI's work.

   A warning sign
   :   I kept the AI text as it was.

       Why: An unchanged AI draft is not your own work.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-12/sims/statement-builder.html" poster="../../week-12/sims/statement-builder.png" title="Statement Builder: say how you used AI" >}}

3. In **Statement Builder**, build an honest statement for Sami's report
   *Water at work*. Which sentence is a warning sign?

   {{< record "The warning sign: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **"I kept the text as it was"**, with a first draft: an unchanged AI
   draft is not your own work. Fix it with "I rewrote it in my own words"
   and "I checked every fact in two reliable sources".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Where does the AI-use statement go?

   - [x] at the end of the work

     Why: The reader sees it when the work is finished.

   - [ ] in a separate e-mail that nobody reads

     Why: The statement belongs to the work itself.

   - [ ] nowhere, if the teacher does not ask

     Why: Honest work always says when AI helped.
   :::
